facts.text: Clinton was named for New York Governor DeWitt Clinton, not the Revolutionary War general as some sources suggest.
The first settlers arrived around 1775, after the area joined the Plymouth Patent, and early pioneers like George FitzGerald and David Gray came from Ireland.
Clinton’s Grange Hall, built in 1915, earned a spot on the National Register of Historic Places, reflecting the town’s agricultural heritage.
A ferry operated across the Kennebec River in the late 18th century, started by Benjamin Noble, and was abandoned about twenty years later.
The Sebasticook River winds north‑south through Clinton, giving the town its own scenic waterway that feeds into the Kennebec.
Clinton is the northernmost town in Kennebec County, with Somerset County towns to its north and west and Waldo County to its east.
